head: claude/night-mi84-mi85-and-the-release-window
title: MI-84 re-measured (17 of 17 inherited rows wrong), MI-85 diagnosed (do NOT close it), MI-86 filed
body:
## Summary

The night shift's substantive work: **MI-84 re-measured**, **MI-85 diagnosed** (and the diagnosis *inverts* the obvious call), and **MI-86 filed** for the defect that cost this session its first 16 minutes.

Checklist-only. One file. No live path, no order path, no register outside `MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json`.

---

## MI-84 — the registry is worse than the 20:52Z reading, not better

**Populations, both sides stated.** Registry: all **82** rows in `SESSIONS.json` @ `origin/main` (48 null, 18 `working`, 14 `idle`, 1 `running`, 1 `archived`). Live: `list_sessions(mine=true, limit=100)` @ 22:00Z returning **100** sessions (2 WORKING, 74 REVIEW_READY, 19 BLOCKED, 4 COMPLETED, 1 FAILED).

**Of the 18 rows the registry calls `working`, live agrees on 1 and disagrees on 17.**

⚠️ **The one it agrees on is this session's own row** — written minutes earlier. Every *inherited* `working` row is wrong: **17 of 17**. And the disagreements aren't all benign idleness: **1 FAILED** (`session_01LqVvgvusnN87neBn5ayzhg` — the session MI-18 records as archived while its item still reads `in_flight`) and **9 BLOCKED**. A manager reading this file sees 18 sessions working for it; 17 are not, and at least 9 are stuck.

⚠️ **Stated limit:** `has_more` was **TRUE**, so 100 is a cap, not the fleet. This does **not** weaken the finding — all 18 registry `working` rows were present in the 100 read (**0 absent**), so the cross-check is complete for every row graded.

**Graded against the live read, not the file**, as the rule requires.

---

## MI-85 — diagnosed against fresh main, and the answer is *not* "close it"

1. **The red was never the blocker.** `mergeable_state` is **`dirty`** — #10398 has a **merge conflict**, which is also the `total_count: 0` signature. Probed by merging fresh `origin/main` into the PR head: conflicts in exactly **2** files, `econ_calendar_snapshots.jsonl` and `econ_calendar_upcoming.json` — both **derived**, both regenerated 4× since (most recently #10711 on 09-02), so main's copies are newer and correct.

2. **The live-path claim is TRUE** — verified against the diff, as MI-85 asked, not against the description. Complete changed-file set **n=3**, all under `comms/macro/`; `config/economic_calendar.yaml` is absent from the diff.

3. ⚠️ **Why it must not be closed as stale.** The capture it carries is a **gap-filler**. `main` holds 36 captures running 08-27, 08-28, then **08-30**, 08-31, 09-01, 09-02 — **2026-08-29 is missing**, and #10398 holds the only copy (main's `snapshots.jsonl` has **0** rows mentioning `20260829`). The naive reading — *"4-day-old PIT data, close it"* — would **permanently lose a day from the point-in-time series**.

4. **The disposition is a judgement call and I deliberately did not take it**, per MI-85's own instruction. The shape of a correct fix: keep the capture (new, unique, unconflicted), take **main's** side of both derived files, then **re-run the producer** — `scripts/macro/econ_calendar_snapshot_backfill.py` exists for exactly this. ⚠️ Hand-resolving a conflict in generated PIT data would **fabricate a snapshot no capture produced**, which is the one thing PIT data must never contain. That is why this is a decision, not a merge.

**Not done:** CI was not re-run against fresh main, because the branch does not merge cleanly and pushing a hand-made resolution is precisely what is being avoided. MI-85 moves to `blocked` on a **dated** basis, not a bare-string claim.

---

## MI-86 — an unpushed *release* strands the successor

Found by living it. The day manager released the lease at **21:38:05Z**; the release reached `origin` at **21:41:54Z** (#10869). This session fetched at **21:39:37Z** — inside that window — read `state=held`, and correctly stood down for 16 minutes.

⚠️ **The guard was right and must not be weakened.** `manager_preflight.py` graded exactly what `origin` showed. The bug is the **freshness of the file**, never the strictness of the check.

**It is structural, not bad luck:** the lease file warns about this window in the *claim* direction (*"a claim you never pushed protects nothing"*). This is the same window in the *release* direction, and it lands in the worst possible place — the outgoing manager releases and spawns its successor in the same breath, so the successor's first read falls inside the window **by construction**.

Secondary lesson, this session's own: a **negative existence claim** ("no release commit exists") from a single read of a store with a known unpushed window **is not a measurement**. It was published to board #6927 and #10871 before being retracted at 21:54Z.

## Architecture impact

- [x] **Not applicable** — checklist rows only.

- [x] Round-trip verified byte-identical at `indent=2` **before** writing, so the diff is surgical (+22/−9) with no reformat noise
- [x] MI-85's `blocked_on_basis` carries a dated observation, satisfying `manager_preflight.py::blocked_claims`
- [ ] CI green

## Filed for follow-ups

- **#10857 merged at 21:59:16Z on auto-merge**, 16s after `pytest-run` went green — **not merged by this session**. `landed_unproven` is correct: no ping has been *seen arriving*.
- **#10859 remains held** on the operator's one Tier-2 OK. Untouched.
- MI-86's fixes are **recorded, not built**.
